title: Quasi-affineness of quasi-compact opens from affine target charts
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $Y=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an affine open cover. Suppose that, for each $i$, every quasi-compact open subscheme of $f^{-1}(U_i)$ is quasi-affine, meaning isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Here quasi-compact means that every open covering admits a finite subcover. Let $V\subseteq Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated open subscheme [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $K\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme. Then the induced morphism $K\to V$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. In particular, if $V$ is affine, $K$ is a quasi-affine scheme. No quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis is imposed on $X$, $Y$, or $f$.

source.place: Tag 0F1U, lemma-ind-quasi-affine-alternative-definition, proof (3) implies (4), with affine-chart scheme formulation from (1) iff (2); Tag 0AP6, definition-ind-quasi-affine

proof.text: Write $h:K\to V$ for the induced morphism. Since $K$ is quasi-compact and $V$ is quasi-separated, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) says that $h$ is quasi-compact. This assertion requires no quasi-compactness or separation of $f$, $X$, or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 03GI, lemma-quasi-compact-permanence, as used in Tag 0F1U

proof.text: For every $v\in V$, choose $i$ with $v\in U_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] to the open subset $V\cap U_i$ of $Y$ and the point $v$, obtaining an affine open $W\subseteq V\cap U_i$ containing $v$. Thus the family of all such pairs $(i,W)$ is an affine open cover of $V$. We do not assert that $V\cap U_i$ itself is affine or quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; affine refinement in Tag 0F1U, (3) implies (4)

proof.text: Fix a member $(i,W)$ of this cover and put $L=h^{-1}(W)=K\cap f^{-1}(W)$. The quasi-compactness of $h$ from step 1 means, by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], that $L$ is quasi-compact, since $W$ is affine. It is an open subscheme of $f^{-1}(U_i)$ because $K$ is open in $f^{-1}(V)$ and $W\subseteq U_i$. The hypothesis on $U_i$ therefore says that the scheme $L$ is quasi-affine.

source.place: Tag 0F1U, lemma-ind-quasi-affine-alternative-definition, proof (3) implies (4); Tag 01K4 affine criterion

proof.text: For every member $W$ of the affine cover in step 2, step 3 proves that $h^{-1}(W)$ is a quasi-affine scheme. The reverse implication of [lem-a1-quasi-affine-target-locality], applied to $h:K\to V$ and this cover, gives that $h$ is quasi-affine.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (1), used in Tag 0F1U

proof.text: If $V$ is affine, use $V$ itself as an affine open of the target in [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. The inverse image $h^{-1}(V)=K$ is then a quasi-affine scheme, proving the final clause.
